page: Microsoft Azure E48s_v6 is an Esv6-family virtual machine configured with 48 dedicated vCPUs and 384.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz, the instance features 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. The CPU architecture is x86_64, supported by a 260 MB L3 cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache. This server does not include local storage or onboard GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark evaluations indicate strong multi-threaded and memory performance. The instance achieved a Geekbench multi-core score of 17316.0 and a Passmark CPU score of 60432.72, both placing in the top 25% tier. Cryptographic and vector processing capabilities are supported by hardware-accelerated instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX), which contributed to a Passmark CPU encryption test score of 47980.09. Large-block read-only memory bandwidth reached 190.66 GB/sec, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression performed at 291.99 GB/sec. However, the Passmark memory score registered in the lower 25% tier at 1645.83.

Given its high memory density and dedicated compute resources, the E48s_v6 is designed for memory-intensive workloads such as relational databases, in-memory caching, and data analytics. It demonstrates strong performance in Redis SET operations, processing 63.01 million operations per second, and static web serving at 78.62 GB/sec. Additionally, the inclusion of AMX instructions enables efficient CPU-based machine learning tasks, as evidenced by strong prompt processing speeds across small, medium, and large language models. The absence of bundled local storage and GPUs makes it a cost-efficient choice for enterprise applications that rely on external Premium Storage and do not require hardware acceleration.
